## Overview **+13.8% decode at c=1 (+7.7% at c=4) from the sparse LM head alone**, with average AL unchanged (+0.1%), on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3) on one DGX Spark. It composes with quantization: +23.3% with NVFP4 rows, and +5.5 to 7.9% on top of a full NVFP4 draft head (#59973) across draft lengths k=3 to 8. On Nemotron 3.5 Lightning MTP (k=7) the draft step is 0.816x of dense with BF16 rows. Addresses #58578. **Why:** an MTP drafter reads the target's full lm_head for every draft token (248k x 2560 in BF16 on Flash-Next), so on bandwidth-bound GPUs the head dominates the draft step, while only a small, context-dependent part of the vocabulary is likely. A fixed list alone loses 5.7% of average AL and 33% on multilingual SPEED-Bench prompts. **How:** the drafter scores a fixed token list plus, per draft token, the rows outside it that score best under a rank-256 projection of the lm_head, and computes exact logits only for those rows. The target still verifies with its full head, so only the acceptance length can change. Opt-in keys in `speculative_config`: `draft_token_map` (SGLang `.pt` or JSON list) and `draft_token_map_dynamic_rows`; with `draft_lm_head_quantization` only the copied rows are quantized. Supported on Qwen3.5, Qwen4Exp and NemotronH MTP. Draft-vocabulary handling moves into model code: one `DraftVocab` helper returns target-vocabulary logits, and EAGLE3, DFlash and DSpark use it instead of their own `draft_id_to_target_id` scatter. ## Results Flash-Next, SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories, 409 requests, greedy, 256 tokens), MTP k=3, FP8 KV, GB10, measured with this branch's fused kernel (3ed5c097f7); each row against its own stock run on the same node: | draft rows (32k list + 16k dynamic) | AL avg | AL multilingual | decode c=1 | decode c=4 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | stock (full BF16 head), mean of the 3 runs | 2.667 | 2.827 | 39.6 tok/s | 26.4 tok/s | | BF16 | +0.1% | -4.7% | +13.8% | +7.7% | | FP8 | -1.1% | -8.1% | +20.6% | +11.0% | | NVFP4 | -0.8% | -6.6% | **+23.3%** | +13.6% | GSM8K (first 200, greedy): stock 98.5%, NVFP4 rows 98.0%. `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, MTP k=7, 8k list + 4k dynamic rows, one GB10 node: | draft head | step time c=1 | real AL | projected decode c=1 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | dense BF16 head | 115.5 ms | 3.734 | baseline | | BF16 rows | 0.816x | 3.656 | +20.0% | | full NVFP4 head (#59973) | 0.828x | 3.676 | +18.9% | | NVFP4 rows | 0.785x | 3.672 | +25.3% (+5.4% over the full NVFP4 head) | The list size depends on the model: the settings measured here are 8k + 4k rows on Nemotron's 131k vocabulary and 32k + 16k on Qwen's 248k. Disclaimers: - Low-concurrency feature: dynamic rows are gathered per token, so the gain shrinks with tokens per step (c=4 above; Lightning at c=8 measured +2.8% aggregate for BF16 rows over dense). - Lightning step time is measured with forced acceptance (AL 3.75, 22 prompts, 1024 tokens); real AL comes from standard rejection at c=8 (44 prompts, up to 4096 tokens); projected decode = real AL / step time. - Multilingual AL drops 5 to 8% on Flash-Next (a static list alone loses 30% or more). - Every comparison is a same-node pair.
Composition with a quantized draft head On top of a full NVFP4 draft head (#59973), NVFP4 rows, BF16 MTP-layer KV, each cell a same-node pair, Flash-Next decode c=1 (c=4): k=3 +5.8% (+3.7%), k=4 +7.5% (+3.7%), k=5 +5.5% (+1.4%), k=6 +6.8% (+2.7%), k=7 +6.1% (+0.5%), k=8 +7.9% (+6.7%), average AL within 1.5%. Same revision as the table above.
Design details - `vllm/model_executor/layers/draft_vocab.py`: `DraftVocab.compute_logits` returns target-vocabulary logits that are `-inf` outside the draft vocabulary; `get_top_tokens` keeps local-argmax greedy drafting without full logits. The subset is either a checkpoint-pruned head with `draft_id_to_target_id` (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) or the `draft_token_map` rows of a shared full head. - MTP drafters share the target lm_head only inside `load_eagle_model`, so the rows are copied right after sharing; that is the one speculator-side hook. - Quantized rows use the platform's weight-only kernels (`init_wfp8_a16_linear_kernel`, `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel`).
This PR does not change verification, add `draft_token_map` to EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark (they already prune in the checkpoint), or support lm_heads quantized in the checkpoint (rejected at load, #60226). `draft_token_map` needs tensor parallel size 1.
Tests ```bash pytest -q tests/model_executor/layers/test_draft_vocab.py tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py pytest -q tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_draft_vocab.py ``` Unit tests pass on GB10 (46 passed) and on the CPU platform (25 passed, 19 skipped as CUDA-only). The e2e test passes on GB10: Qwen3.5-0.8B MTP AL 1.912 stock and 1.912 with a 32k list + 1k dynamic rows, GSM8K above the reference threshold. New tests cover the pruned-head id mapping, listed and dynamic rows, FP8/NVFP4 rows, and NemotronH MTP drafting over a token map (CPU). Re-check after merging main (ca5c2d7843), same GB10 node, c=1, 22 SPEED-Bench prompts, 256 tokens, real AL: Flash-Next k=3, 32k + 16k BF16 rows vs stock: decode 46.8 vs 40.8 tok/s (+14.6%), AL 2.706 vs 2.736, step 0.862x; Lightning k=7, 8k + 4k BF16 rows vs dense: decode 46.0 vs 37.8 tok/s (+21.6%), AL 4.302 vs 4.360, step 0.811x.
**Not a duplicate.** #24343 and #29334 (FR-Spec, static lists only) were closed unmerged. #59973 quantizes the full draft head; this cuts the rows read, and the two compose. The NemotronH `get_top_tokens` added here overlaps #59727, which adds the same method without a draft vocabulary. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above.
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

Hi @stecasta, we tried this on our TP2 setup (2× DGX Spark, eager, MTP k=4, nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, MRV2) with dynamic rows extended to TP>1. Two things came up:

1. **Splitting the list by vocab shard leaves it almost entirely on rank 0.** Frequent tokens have low ids: with the Qwen tokenizer on ~17M tokens of code/docs, 97% of a top-32k frequency list falls in the first half of the vocab. So at TP2 the static part doesn't shrink. Splitting the sorted list into equal contiguous chunks (each rank fetches the rows it doesn't own once at load, with one all-reduce) fixes that and keeps the gathered columns in sorted-id order, so `restrict`/`scatter`/`to_target` are unchanged.
2. **Dynamic rows at TP>1:** we all-reduce the Gram once so every rank uses the same basis. Each rank picks `ceil(rows / tp)` off-list rows from its own shard, and greedy drafting reduces local `(logit, id)` pairs with one small all-gather, so no per-token id exchange is needed. Probabilistic drafting with dynamic rows is still rejected at TP>1.

Results (32k list = ids 0..32767 + added tokens, greedy 1024-token decode, each arm a fresh start):

| draft head | decode c=1 | AL |
|---|---:|---:|
| BF16 full head | 36.9 tok/s | 2.693 |
| FP8 full head (#56577) | 43.7 | 2.693 |
| 32k + 16k dynamic (8k/rank) | 44.8 | 2.695 |
| 32k + 32k dynamic (16k/rank) | 44.0 | 2.695 |

Greedy outputs were byte-identical across arms. That's about +21% over the BF16 head at TP2 with no AL loss on our prompts, though only marginal over an FP8 full head at TP2. At c=4 the dynamic arms were within run-to-run noise of the FP8 head. Your existing tests pass unchanged; the by-shard layout test is replaced by emulated-TP2 tests for the balanced split and the dynamic-row argmax (17/17 on CPU).

If it's useful, I can rebase this onto your branch and push it for you to pull in.

Thanks @kosztyua, great data, and good to see +21% at TP2 with byte-identical outputs. Heads-up: I just refactored the PR per review (the draft vocabulary now lives in model code as a shared `DraftVocab`, and `restrict`/`scatter`/`to_target` are gone from the speculator), so your patch won't apply as is. To keep this PR reviewable I'd like to land it with dynamic rows at TP=1 first. Would you be up for opening the balanced split and TP>1 dynamic rows as a follow-up on top once it lands? Happy to review it.

Thanks, landing TP=1 first makes sense. The follow-up is low priority on my side for now: on our TP2 setup we already run a quantized draft head, and on top of that the gain was within noise. I might get to it eventually, but in case anyone else wants to pick up TP>1 first, here are the two things that mattered:

- **Static list:** split it into equal contiguous chunks of the sorted list rather than sharding it by vocab. With a frequency-sorted list, vocab sharding puts ~97% of it on rank 0, so TP2 barely shrinks the static part.
- **Dynamic rows:** all-reduce the Gram matrix once so every rank uses the same basis. Each rank then picks ceil(rows/tp) of its own shard's off-list rows, and greedy drafting reduces the local (logit, id) pairs with one small all-gather. I rejected probabilistic drafting with dynamic rows at TP>1.

At TP2 that gave +21% over a stock BF16 head with byte-identical outputs. Happy to answer questions or review if someone takes it on.

Really nice work — the context-aware dynamic rows (static 32k + per-token rank-256-SVD-picked 16k) and the quantization composition are a meaningfully better design than what we tried; measuring on the multilingual-AL cost of a static-only list is exactly the kind of detail that would've bitten us if we'd gone further down that road.

(I'm BRANTD-veta, posting for VENETA — the repo linked below is ours.)

We hit this same general idea from a different angle tonight and landed in a spot that might be useful context, since our numbers on the same model/hardware differ from yours by a fair amount and I don't want that sitting unexplained: static-list-only, on `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` + MTP k=3 on one DGX Spark, we (or rather the kit we built on, MiaAI-Lab's) measured +54% decode, versus your +15.2% (BF16, c=1) / +22.6% (NVFP4). We're not asserting a cause for the gap — different prompt sets, concurrency, baseline choice, and static-vs-dynamic rows are all plausible and we haven't isolated which — but wanted to flag the discrepancy rather than let two very different numbers for what sounds like the same mechanism go uncommented in either of our writeups.

Separately, and maybe more useful here: we measured the static-list idea on two model classes your changed-files list doesn't touch — plain EAGLE (`yuhuili/EAGLE-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` on Llama 3.1 8B: +13.4% decode, 15.83 → 17.95 tok/s, same acceptance, zero output difference) and a native-MTP-head model whose class has no `get_top_tokens()` override at all, EXAONE 4.5's `Exaone4_5_MTP`. Both go through the same `DraftModelSpeculator`/`AutoRegressiveSpeculator` dispatch your PR's eagle/utils.py hook also touches, so the same shape of fix (slice `lm_head` into a fresh tensor, attach `get_top_tokens()`, never write back into the shared weight) covers them without needing your dynamic-rows machinery — simpler, but also not in the same league on multilingual degradation, since we only tested a static list.

Full writeup and numbers: https://github.com/veneta-ai/mtp-draft-vocab-ko. Credit to this PR and #58578 for the idea and the much more sophisticated implementation here — not trying to claim priority on the general concept, just filling in a couple of model classes this PR doesn't reach yet. Happy to open a small, separate PR for that narrower piece if it's useful, rather than scope-creeping this one.

Thanks for the additional context @BRANTD-veta

1. About the +54%: We are measuring different things. From your results/README the baseline is the kit's en+code 47k list on Korean prompts (AL 1.33), and the other arm is a Korean-extended 65k list (2.16). So it's list vs list on a language the baseline doesn't cover, while ours is vs the full BF16 head on SPEED-Bench. Your numbers actually match what we see: a static list collapses on languages it doesn't cover, and a per-language list fixes it. The context-aware rows are there so we don't need a file per language

2. About the other model classes: the current head moves this into a shared `DraftVocab` helper in model code. EAGLE3, DFlash and DSpark already use it, and MTP models opt in with a few lines (see `qwen3_5_mtp.py`). Plain EAGLE, `exaone4_5_mtp`, `glm4_moe_mtp` and `deepseek_mtp` are not wired yet. I'd rather not add a second mechanism that attaches `get_top_tokens()` per instance, but a follow-up wiring those models to the same helper would be great. Happy to review it once this lands!

Thanks @stecasta — both points land.

1. Agreed on the +54%: that's list-vs-list on a language the baseline doesn't cover, not static-list-vs-full-head — same framing we use in our own README, just stated more plainly here.

2. Agreed on one mechanism rather than two. We'd rather wire the four models we measured (plain EAGLE, `exaone4_5_mtp`, `glm4_moe_mtp`, `deepseek_mtp`) into your shared `DraftVocab` helper instead of keeping our own attach-at-load approach. We'll open that as a follow-up once this lands, and expect to close #60387 at that point rather than leave two overlapping PRs for reviewers to reconcile. Will ping you on the follow-up.
Confirming on our side — we'll start the plain-EAGLE / `exaone4_5_mtp` / `glm4_moe_mtp` / `deepseek_mtp` follow-up as soon as this merges, and close #60387 at that point. Watching for the merge.

Since a few more people are following this thread now, here's the fuller picture on our side — thanks for the patience with a longer comment.

**What we're actually trying to fix.** We didn't start from this PR's mechanism; we started from a narrower problem. The draft vocabularies shipped today (this PR's included, and the kit we built on) are frequency-ranked on English and code. That's not a neutral default — it means speculative decoding speeds up English the most and helps non-English speakers the least, by construction, unless someone extends the list for their language. We built a Korean 65k file for `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` first (+54% decode on Korean prompts over the shipped en+code list, acceptance 1.33 → 2.16, zero replacement characters) and are extending the same recipe to roughly 19 more languages across Asia, Africa and the Western languages not yet covered. It's a non-profit, public-interest effort on our side — no customer data, no paid product behind it, Apache-2.0: https://github.com/veneta-ai/mtp-draft-vocab-ko.

**What we learned here.** Three things changed how we think about this: the context-aware dynamic rows (static list + per-token rank-256-SVD-picked rows) are a real answer to the exact problem we have — a per-language static file is a workaround, not a fix, and this design doesn't need one; @kosztyua's TP>1 data caught a failure mode we hadn't tested for yet (sharding a frequency-sorted list by vocab range puts ~97% of it on one rank, so naive TP>1 barely shrinks anything — the fix is a balanced contiguous-chunk split); and @stecasta's read of our own +54% number was right — that's list-vs-list on a language the baseline doesn't cover, not a speedup over an unrestricted head, and worth saying plainly rather than letting readers assume the bigger claim.

**Our plan once this merges.** We'll open a follow-up PR wiring the four model classes we've measured — plain EAGLE (`yuhuili/EAGLE-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` on Llama 3.1 8B, +13.4% decode), `exaone4_5_mtp` (EXAONE 4.5, +7.0%), `glm4_moe_mtp`, and `deepseek_mtp` — into the shared `DraftVocab` helper rather than keep our own attach-at-load mechanism around. #60387 closes once that's up. We're watching for the merge and will follow up here.

Thanks again — @stecasta, @kosztyua, @benchislett — for a thread that taught us more about this than we'd have worked out alone.

Field report from a single-card deployment, in case it helps the review.

We have run this PR in production since 2026-10-07: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (RadixArk NVFP4 checkpoint) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB), v0.31.0 with this PR applied, MTP K=2 with an NVFP4 drafter plus a static 64K draft vocab map (`draft_token_map_quantization: nvfp4`), 6 seats, prefix caching on, FP8 KV. It serves daily traffic from coding agents and Hermes agent tasks, almost all English (under 1% Chinese). We have had no crashes or stability issues attributable to it, and a teacher-forced logprob check with prefix caching off matched builds without it.

Today we ran a one-variable A/B on the same image and flags, removing only `draft_token_map`/`draft_token_map_quantization`. Each side was benchmarked on an idle server. Decode used 512 output tokens with `ignore_eos`, warmed prefixes and synthetic filler prompts. Parallel rows give total tok/s and are the median of 3 bursts.

| | with map | without map | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 stream, 256 / 16K / 128K ctx | 153.6 / 144.3 / 130.8 | 139.9 / 125.8 / 119.3 | +10% / +15% / +10% |
| 2 streams, 256 / 16K / 100K ctx | 267 / 234 / 230 | 244 / 213 / 215 | +9% / +10% / +7% |
| 4 streams, 256 / 16K / 100K ctx | 455 / 352 / 350 | 427 / 334 / 344 | +7% / +5% / +2% |
| 6 streams, 256 / 16K ctx | 578 / 411 | 566 / 410 | +2% / 0% |
| MTP acceptance (sweep) | 52.9% | 54.1% | ~same |
| KV pool | 715,653 | 723,517 | -1% |

On this card the gain comes from a cheaper draft step, not from acceptance, which is unchanged within noise. It is largest at low concurrency (about +10-15% for a single stream) and shrinks to roughly zero at 6 concurrent streams, where the target forward dominates. The map costs about 8K tokens of KV pool.

Happy to rerun on a rebased head if that would be useful.

**Update (same day):** the PR also rebases onto the v0.32.0 tag with one trivial conflict (an import line in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/mtp.py`, both sides kept). With the same flags and map on v0.32.0, speed matched the v0.31.0 build within noise (+2-3% total at 6 streams), MTP acceptance was unchanged (52.9%), and the prefix-off logprob check matched (-0.4231 vs -0.4278, n=8). Production now runs on v0.32.0 with this PR applied.

Thanks for posting this. A one-variable A/B on the same image and flags, with the acceptance row and the KV pool delta next to the throughput, is a lot more than a review usually gets to see.

Corroboration from our side, on a **different implementation** of the same idea (#60387, the `get_top_tokens()` variant) and different hardware, which lands inside your single-stream band:

- Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE-1, k=3, 65,536 of 128,256 ids kept: 18.13 → 20.48 tok/s (**+12.9%**)
- EXAONE 4.5 33B FP8, native MTP head, k=3: 5.37 → 5.92 tok/s (**+10.3%**)

Conditions for both: one GB10, TP=1, temp 0, 20 fixed Korean prompts × 3 repeats (n=60 per arm), median decode, **single stream**. Acceptance was flat across arms (1.70–1.71 and 1.07 accepted/draft), and the drafter's `lm_head` read shrank 1002 → 512 MiB. That is why we also concluded the gain is a cheaper draft step rather than better drafts, so your "cheaper draft step, not acceptance" reading matches ours on a different model, precision, language and implementation.

Your concurrency curve is the part we had not measured, and it is the test that explanation needed. If the win is draft-step cost, it has to shrink once the target forward dominates the step, which is what your 4- and 6-stream rows show. Had it stayed near +12% at 6 streams, the cheaper-draft-step story would have been wrong and something else would have been going on. We are adding "single stream" to our own numbers on the strength of it.

One question, since you offered to rerun. Every parallel row is a median of 3 bursts, but the acceptance row has no repeat count, and it is the one row where the map comes out slightly behind (52.9% against 54.1%). At 6 streams the throughput gain is already about zero, while the ~8K tokens of KV pool and any real acceptance difference do not go away, so the sign of the net at high concurrency depends on whether that 1.2 points is noise. If a rerun is cheap, acceptance measured the same way as the throughput rows (median of 3) at 1 and 6 streams would settle it, and it is the number most likely to come up in review.

Worth noting that the branch has had merge conflicts flagged since 2026-10-12, so a rebase is needed regardless. A rerun could ride along with it.

@BRANTD-veta good catch on the acceptance row. Short answer first, details below: measured per burst, the map arm is about 1 point lower in acceptance at 6 streams, within burst noise, and still ahead on throughput there.

Why the original row had no repeat count: each acceptance value was one cumulative counter read at the end of a sweep, and the two sides came from separate sweeps.

Rerun today on the v0.32.0 + #59740 build with production flags. The two arms differ only in `draft_token_map`/`draft_token_map_quantization` and ran back to back on an idle server. Acceptance per burst is the delta of `spec_decode_num_accepted/draft_tokens_total` across that burst alone. Each cell is the median of 5 bursts (you suggested 3; 5 cost little extra), with the burst range in brackets. Per burst: 512 tokens per stream, `ignore_eos`, warmed prefixes, synthetic filler, temperature 0.7.

| ctx, streams | accept, with map | accept, without map | total tok/s, with / without |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256, 1 | 54.3% (47.0-57.1) | 55.1% (52.6-55.6) | 158.3 / 141.5 |
| 256, 6 | 51.9% (46.9-54.9) | 53.0% (51.4-54.3) | 582.7 / 537.0 |
| 16K, 1 | 52.0% (45.7-53.4) | 51.8% (46.4-53.4) | 144.4 / 130.0 |
| 16K, 6 | 51.8% (51.0-53.9) | 52.9% (51.1-54.9) | 412.5 / 394.9 |

At 6 streams the map arm is about 1 point lower in acceptance (mean 51.9% vs 52.9% over 10 bursts per arm, t = -1.3). A separate with-map run earlier the same morning gave 52.4% and 52.0% at 6 streams, so the direction repeats, but the gap is within burst noise and I would not call it established. At 1 stream, single bursts within one cell span up to 13 points (8-13 for the map runs, 3-7 without the map), so the medians there do not separate the arms.

Net at 6 streams: the map was still ahead on throughput, +8.5% at 256 ctx and +4.5% at 16K. At 256 ctx each arm had one slow burst (about 390 tok/s); the other four bursts do not overlap (576-594 with the map, 535-562 without). At 16K the ranges just touch (405.6-416.1 vs 387.7-408.6). Our earlier session on v0.31.0 showed +2% / 0% at 6 streams, so the size of the gain varies by a few percent between sessions. My reading: the map may cost about a point of acceptance, plausibly because target tokens outside the 64K subset can never be drafted (not verified in code), and that cost does not turn the net negative at 6 streams on this card.

Nice to see the conflicts gone and two more classes wired. Two shapes are still uncovered, and they are the two I happen to have measurements for, so here is what I have — and an offer.

**I can wire `exaone4_5_mtp.py` into `DraftVocab`.** It owns a `ParallelLMHead`, so it fits the 4–8 line pattern this PR already applies to eleven classes. I would rather open that against this PR than keep a second mechanism alive. Say the word and it is yours.

**The one I cannot wire that way: EAGLE-1.** `vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle.py` has no `lm_head` of its own — the only mention of one in the module is `if "lm_head" not in name:` while loading weights, because that drafter shares the target's head. The per-model pattern passes `self.lm_head` into the helper, so for this shape there is nothing to hook.

So the design question, which is really the only thing I am asking: is a generic fallback on `DraftModelSpeculator` the intended answer for drafters without their own head — that is what #60387 does — or would you rather have a different hook? Either answer works for me. What I would like to avoid is the project carrying two mechanisms for one idea.

**Why these two shapes are worth the trouble:**

| arm | decode | class |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE-1, k=3, 65,536 of 128,256 ids | 18.13 → 20.48 tok/s (**+12.9 %**) | `llama_eagle.py`, unwired |
| EXAONE 4.5 33B FP8, native MTP head, k=3 | 5.37 → 5.92 tok/s (**+10.3 %**) | `exaone4_5_mtp.py`, unwired |

Conditions for both: one GB10, TP=1, temp 0, 20 fixed prompts × 3 repeats (n = 60 per arm), median decode, **single stream**. Acceptance flat across arms (1.70–1.71 and 1.07 accepted/draft); the drafter's `lm_head` read shrank 1002 → 512 MiB. So the gain is a cheaper draft step, not better drafts.

That reading is the same one @chuang44-tiff's production numbers above support, on different hardware, a different model and a different implementation: +10–15 % at one stream, acceptance unchanged, decaying to about zero at six concurrent streams. ## Overview **+13.8% decode at c=1 (+7.7% at c=4) from the sparse LM head alone**, with average AL unchanged (+0.1%), on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3) on one DGX Spark. It composes with quantization: +23.3% with NVFP4 rows, and +5.5 to 7.9% on top of a full NVFP4 draft head (#59973) across draft lengths k=3 to 8. On Nemotron 3.5 Lightning MTP (k=7) the draft step is 0.816x of dense with BF16 rows. Addresses #58578. **Why:** an MTP drafter reads the target's full lm_head for every draft token (248k x 2560 in BF16 on Flash-Next), so on bandwidth-bound GPUs the head dominates the draft step, while only a small, context-dependent part of the vocabulary is likely. A fixed list alone loses 5.7% of average AL and 33% on multilingual SPEED-Bench prompts. **How:** the drafter scores a fixed token list plus, per draft token, the rows outside it that score best under a rank-256 projection of the lm_head, and computes exact logits only for those rows. The target still verifies with its full head, so only the acceptance length can change. Opt-in keys in `speculative_config`: `draft_token_map` (SGLang `.pt` or JSON list) and `draft_token_map_dynamic_rows`; with `draft_lm_head_quantization` only the copied rows are quantized. Supported on Qwen3.5, Qwen4Exp and NemotronH MTP. Draft-vocabulary handling moves into model code: one `DraftVocab` helper returns target-vocabulary logits, and EAGLE3, DFlash and DSpark use it instead of their own `draft_id_to_target_id` scatter. ## Results Flash-Next, SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories, 409 requests, greedy, 256 tokens), MTP k=3, FP8 KV, GB10, measured with this branch's fused kernel (3ed5c097f7); each row against its own stock run on the same node: | draft rows (32k list + 16k dynamic) | AL avg | AL multilingual | decode c=1 | decode c=4 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | stock (full BF16 head), mean of the 3 runs | 2.667 | 2.827 | 39.6 tok/s | 26.4 tok/s | | BF16 | +0.1% | -4.7% | +13.8% | +7.7% | | FP8 | -1.1% | -8.1% | +20.6% | +11.0% | | NVFP4 | -0.8% | -6.6% | **+23.3%** | +13.6% | GSM8K (first 200, greedy): stock 98.5%, NVFP4 rows 98.0%. `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, MTP k=7, 8k list + 4k dynamic rows, one GB10 node: | draft head | step time c=1 | real AL | projected decode c=1 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | dense BF16 head | 115.5 ms | 3.734 | baseline | | BF16 rows | 0.816x | 3.656 | +20.0% | | full NVFP4 head (#59973) | 0.828x | 3.676 | +18.9% | | NVFP4 rows | 0.785x | 3.672 | +25.3% (+5.4% over the full NVFP4 head) | The list size depends on the model: the settings measured here are 8k + 4k rows on Nemotron's 131k vocabulary and 32k + 16k on Qwen's 248k. Disclaimers: - Low-concurrency feature: dynamic rows are gathered per token, so the gain shrinks with tokens per step (c=4 above; Lightning at c=8 measured +2.8% aggregate for BF16 rows over dense). - Lightning step time is measured with forced acceptance (AL 3.75, 22 prompts, 1024 tokens); real AL comes from standard rejection at c=8 (44 prompts, up to 4096 tokens); projected decode = real AL / step time. - Multilingual AL drops 5 to 8% on Flash-Next (a static list alone loses 30% or more). - Every comparison is a same-node pair.
Composition with a quantized draft head On top of a full NVFP4 draft head (#59973), NVFP4 rows, BF16 MTP-layer KV, each cell a same-node pair, Flash-Next decode c=1 (c=4): k=3 +5.8% (+3.7%), k=4 +7.5% (+3.7%), k=5 +5.5% (+1.4%), k=6 +6.8% (+2.7%), k=7 +6.1% (+0.5%), k=8 +7.9% (+6.7%), average AL within 1.5%. Same revision as the table above.
Design details - `vllm/model_executor/layers/draft_vocab.py`: `DraftVocab.compute_logits` returns target-vocabulary logits that are `-inf` outside the draft vocabulary; `get_top_tokens` keeps local-argmax greedy drafting without full logits. The subset is either a checkpoint-pruned head with `draft_id_to_target_id` (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark) or the `draft_token_map` rows of a shared full head. - MTP drafters share the target lm_head only inside `load_eagle_model`, so the rows are copied right after sharing; that is the one speculator-side hook. - Quantized rows use the platform's weight-only kernels (`init_wfp8_a16_linear_kernel`, `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel`).

+## Reduced draft vocabulary
+
+MTP heads usually share the target model's lm_head, so every draft token pays
+for a projection onto the full vocabulary. For large vocabularies on
+bandwidth-bound GPUs this can be a large share of the drafting cost. The
+`draft_token_map` key restricts the drafter's head to a list of frequent token
+ids (the [FR-Spec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14856) idea):
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <mtp-model> \
+    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
+                           "draft_token_map": "draft_vocab.pt"}'
+```
+
+- Requires Model Runner V2 (the default on CUDA).
+- Only drafting changes. The target still verifies with its full lm_head, so a
+  token outside the list costs a rejected draft, never a different output
+  distribution. With probabilistic drafting
+  (`draft_sample_method: "probabilistic"`), the proposal is a distribution over
+  the full vocabulary with zero mass outside the list, so rejection sampling
+  stays exact.
+- The file is SGLang's `--speculative-token-map` format (a `.pt` list of ids)
+  or a JSON list. EOS ids are always added.
+- The drafter must share the target's unquantized lm_head, at tensor parallel
+  size 1. Drafters whose model code builds a `DraftVocab` support it (Qwen3.5,
+  Qwen4Exp and NemotronH MTP); others raise an error.
+- Acceptance drops when the list misses tokens your traffic uses, so build it
+  from representative text, ideally the model's own outputs, and include all
+  special tokens. [`build_draft_token_map.py`](../../../examples/features/speculative_decoding/build_draft_token_map.py)
+  ranks token ids by frequency over a corpus.
+  Measure the real acceptance length (see
+  [acceptance metrics](acceptance_metrics.md)) with and without the list.
+
+A static list loses acceptance on traffic it was not built from (for example
+other languages). `draft_token_map_dynamic_rows` adds that many tokens per
+draft step on top of the list: the rows outside the list are scored with a
+rank-256 projection of the lm_head, built from its weights at load time, and
+the best ones get exact logits.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <mtp-model> \
+    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
+                           "draft_token_map": "draft_vocab_32k.pt",
+                           "draft_token_map_dynamic_rows": 16384}'
+```
+
+It costs more per draft token than the list alone, and that cost grows with
+batch size, so measure decode speed at your concurrency.
+
+With `draft_lm_head_quantization` (see the notes below) only the listed and
+dynamic rows are quantized (weight-only), not a full copy of the head; the
+dynamic rows' scorer is then stored in FP8.
+
 ## Notes
 
 - MTP only works for model families that support MTP in vLLM.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Build a frequency-ranked draft vocabulary for `draft_token_map`.
+
+Counts token frequencies over text files and keeps the most frequent ids plus
+every special and added token. The text should look like the traffic you
+serve, ideally text the target model generated.
+
+Example:
+    python examples/features/speculative_decoding/build_draft_token_map.py \\
+        --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --text-file my_outputs.jsonl \\
+        --num-tokens 32768 --output draft_vocab.pt
+
+    vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --speculative-config \\
+        '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
+          "draft_token_map": "draft_vocab.pt"}'
+
+The `.pt` output uses SGLang's `--speculative-token-map` format; a `.json`
+output is also accepted by vLLM.
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+
+import torch
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("--tokenizer", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--text-file",
+        action="append",
+        required=True,
+        help="Plain text, or .jsonl with one string per line; may be repeated.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--num-tokens", type=int, default=32768)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, help=".pt or .json")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.tokenizer)
+    counts: Counter[int] = Counter()
+    for path in args.text_file:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            texts = (
+                [json.loads(line) for line in f]
+                if path.endswith(".jsonl")
+                else [f.read()]
+            )
+        for text in texts:
+            counts.update(tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False))
+
+    keep = set(tokenizer.all_special_ids) | set(tokenizer.get_added_vocab().values())
+    for token_id, _ in counts.most_common():
+        if len(keep) >= args.num_tokens:
+            break
+        keep.add(token_id)
+    ids = sorted(keep)
+
+    if args.output.endswith(".json"):
+        with open(args.output, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(ids, f)
+    else:
+        torch.save(ids, args.output)
+    print(f"Wrote {len(ids)} ids ({len(counts)} distinct ids seen) to {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Draft lm_heads that cover a subset of the target vocabulary.
+
+`DraftVocab` serves two kinds of drafters:
+
+- Checkpoints with a pruned draft lm_head and `draft_id_to_target_id` offsets
+  (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark). This used to live in each model file.
+- MTP drafters that share the target's full lm_head, restricted at load time
+  by `speculative_config.draft_token_map`. On bandwidth-bound GPUs the full
+  head dominates the draft step, so each draft token computes exact logits
+  only for:
+  1. the listed rows, a fixed list of frequent tokens, and
+  2. optionally `draft_token_map_dynamic_rows` more rows per draft token,
+     picked by a rank-256 projection of the lm_head (built from its weights
+     at load time), which recovers what the list misses, e.g. other languages.
+
+Either way `compute_logits` returns target-vocabulary logits that are `-inf`
+outside the subset, so speculators need no special handling. The target still
+verifies with its full head, so only the acceptance length can change.
+"""

+_UNQUANTIZED = (UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
+# Rank of the lm_head projection that scores the dynamic rows. On Qwen3.8
+# MTP, rank 256 alone puts 97.5% of the greedy draft tokens in its top 16k.
+_DYNAMIC_RANK = 256

+def load_draft_token_ids(path: str, extra_ids: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Load a draft token map and return its sorted, unique target ids.
+
+    Args:
+        path: SGLang `--speculative-token-map` file (`.pt`) or a JSON list.
+        extra_ids: Ids that are always included, e.g. EOS.
+
+    Returns:
+        int64 CPU tensor of target token ids.
+
+    """
+    if path.endswith(".json"):
+        with open(path) as f:
+            ids = json.load(f)
+    else:
+        ids = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
+        if isinstance(ids, torch.Tensor):
+            ids = ids.flatten().tolist()
+    if not isinstance(ids, (list, tuple)):
+        raise ValueError(f"draft_token_map {path!r} must hold a flat list of ids.")
+
+    token_ids = torch.tensor([int(i) for i in ids] + extra_ids, dtype=torch.int64)
+    if token_ids.numel() == 0:
+        raise ValueError("draft_token_map is empty.")
+    return torch.unique(token_ids, sorted=True)
+
+
+# Rows per step when copying or quantizing lm_head rows, which bounds the
+# temporaries.
+_CHUNK = 16384
+
+
+def _quantize_rows(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, quantization: str, ids: torch.Tensor | None = None
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+    """Weight-only quantized `weight[ids]` (all rows by default).
+
+    Returns `(fp8_rows, row_scales)` for "fp8" and
+    `(packed_e2m1, e4m3_block_scales, global_scale)` for "nvfp4". The NVFP4
+    global scale covers all of `weight`, so any subset quantizes the same way.
+    """
+    if ids is None:
+        ids = torch.arange(weight.shape[0], device=weight.device)
+    if quantization == "nvfp4":
+        fp4_fp8_max = FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX * torch.finfo(torch.float8_e4m3fn).max
+        global_scale = fp4_fp8_max / weight_amax(weight).float().clamp(min=1e-12)
+    out: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    for start in range(0, ids.numel(), _CHUNK):
+        rows = weight[ids[start : start + _CHUNK]]
+        if quantization == "fp8":
+            parts = ops.scaled_fp8_quant(rows, use_per_token_if_dynamic=True)
+        else:
+            parts = ops.scaled_fp4_quant(
+                rows, global_scale, is_sf_swizzled_layout=False
+            )
+        if not out:
+            out = [p.new_empty(ids.numel(), *p.shape[1:]) for p in parts]
+        for dst, part in zip(out, parts):
+            dst[start : start + part.shape[0]] = part
+    return tuple(out) if quantization == "fp8" else (*out, 1.0 / global_scale)
+
+
+class _Rows(ReplicatedLinear):
+    """lm_head rows as a linear layer, optionally weight-only quantized.
+
+    FP8 keeps one scale per row and NVFP4 one E4M3 scale per 16 weights; both
+    run on the platform's weight-only kernel.
+    """
+
+    weight: nn.Parameter
+
+    def __init__(self, weight: torch.Tensor, quantization: str | None):
+        with torch.device(weight.device):
+            super().__init__(
+                weight.shape[1],
+                weight.shape[0],
+                bias=False,
+                params_dtype=weight.dtype,
+                return_bias=False,
+                disable_tp=True,
+            )
+        self.kernel: FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel | NvFp4LinearKernel | None = None
+        if quantization is None:
+            self.weight_loader(self.weight, weight)
+            self.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(self)
+            return
+        from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear import (
+            init_nvfp4_linear_kernel,
+            init_wfp8_a16_linear_kernel,
+        )
+
+        # What a quantization scheme sets on its layer in create_weights.
+        self.input_size_per_partition = self.input_size
+        self.output_size_per_partition = self.output_size
+        self.logical_widths = self.output_partition_sizes
+        self.orig_dtype = self.params_dtype
+        quantized = _quantize_rows(weight, quantization)
+        if quantization == "fp8":
+            self.kernel = init_wfp8_a16_linear_kernel(
+                weight_quant_key=kFp8StaticChannelSym,
+                activation_quant_key=kFp8DynamicTensorSym,
+                weight_shape=tuple(weight.shape),
+                input_dtype=weight.dtype,
+                out_dtype=weight.dtype,
+            )
+            # The scaled-mm kernels take the weight as (K, N), tagged as such.
+            self.weight = nn.Parameter(quantized[0].t(), requires_grad=False)
+            self.weight.input_dim = 0
+            self.weight.output_dim = 1
+            self.weight_scale = nn.Parameter(quantized[1], requires_grad=False)
+            self.input_scale = None
+            self.weight_block_size = None
+        else:
+            self.kernel = init_nvfp4_linear_kernel(use_a16=True)
+            self.weight = nn.Parameter(quantized[0], requires_grad=False)
+            self.weight_scale = nn.Parameter(quantized[1], requires_grad=False)
+            self.weight_global_scale = nn.Parameter(quantized[2], requires_grad=False)
+        self.kernel.process_weights_after_loading(self)
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:  # type: ignore[override]
+        if self.kernel is None:
+            return self.quant_method.apply(self, x)
+        return self.kernel.apply_weights(self, x)
+
+
+# The two kernels below compute `x[n] @ weight[ids[n, j]]` for the dynamic
+# rows, reading only the picked rows instead of gathering them into a copy.
+# One program handles BLOCK_ROWS picked rows of one token.
+@triton.jit
+def _gather_rows_gemv_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    weight_ptr,
+    scale_ptr,
+    ids_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    num_rows,
+    hidden_size,
+    weight_stride,
+    HAS_SCALE: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_HIDDEN: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    rows = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK_ROWS + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_ROWS)
+    row_mask = rows < num_rows
+    ids = tl.load(ids_ptr + token * num_rows + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_ROWS,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    for start in range(0, hidden_size, BLOCK_HIDDEN):
+        cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_HIDDEN)
+        col_mask = cols < hidden_size
+        x = tl.load(x_ptr + token * hidden_size + cols, mask=col_mask, other=0.0)
+        w = tl.load(
+            weight_ptr + ids[:, None].to(tl.int64) * weight_stride + cols[None, :],
+            mask=row_mask[:, None] & col_mask[None, :],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        acc += tl.sum(w.to(tl.float32) * x[None, :].to(tl.float32), axis=1)
+    if HAS_SCALE:
+        acc *= tl.load(scale_ptr + ids, mask=row_mask, other=0.0)
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + token * num_rows + rows,
+        acc.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=row_mask,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gather_rows_gemv_nvfp4_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    packed_ptr,
+    scale_ptr,
+    global_scale_ptr,
+    ids_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    num_rows,
+    hidden_size,
+    packed_stride,
+    scale_stride,
+    BLOCK_ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_BYTES: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    rows = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK_ROWS + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_ROWS)
+    row_mask = rows < num_rows
+    ids = tl.load(ids_ptr + token * num_rows + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0)
+    ids = ids.to(tl.int64)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_ROWS,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    num_bytes = hidden_size // 2
+    for start in range(0, num_bytes, BLOCK_BYTES):
+        bcols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_BYTES)
+        bmask = bcols < num_bytes
+        mask = row_mask[:, None] & bmask[None, :]
+        # Each byte packs two E2M1 values (low nibble first) and every 8 bytes
+        # (16 values) share one E4M3 block scale.
+        b = tl.load(
+            packed_ptr + ids[:, None] * packed_stride + bcols[None, :],
+            mask=mask,
+            other=0,
+        ).to(tl.int32)
+        sc = tl.load(
+            scale_ptr + ids[:, None] * scale_stride + (bcols // 8)[None, :],
+            mask=mask,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        x_ptrs = x_ptr + token * hidden_size + 2 * bcols
+        x_lo = tl.load(x_ptrs, mask=bmask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+        x_hi = tl.load(x_ptrs + 1, mask=bmask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+        v_lo = _e2m1_inline(b & 15)
+        v_hi = _e2m1_inline((b >> 4) & 15)
+        acc += tl.sum((v_lo * x_lo[None, :] + v_hi * x_hi[None, :]) * sc, axis=1)
+    acc *= tl.load(global_scale_ptr)
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + token * num_rows + rows,
+        acc.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=row_mask,
+    )
+
+
+def gather_rows_gemv(
+    x: torch.Tensor, rows: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], ids: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`out[n, j] = x[n] @ weight[ids[n, j]]` without materializing the rows.
+
+    Args:
+        x: Activations, shape `(N, H)`.
+        rows: `(weight,)` in the activation dtype, `(fp8_weight, row_scale)`
+            or `(nvfp4_packed, block_scales, global_scale)`.
+        ids: Row ids per token, shape `(N, J)`.
+
+    """
+    if not x.is_cuda:
+        assert len(rows) == 1, "quantized rows need CUDA"
+        return torch.einsum("nd,njd->nj", x, rows[0][ids])
+    num_tokens, num_rows = ids.shape
+    out = x.new_empty(num_tokens, num_rows)
+    grid = (num_tokens, triton.cdiv(num_rows, 64))
+    if len(rows) == 3:
+        packed, scales, global_scale = rows
+        _gather_rows_gemv_nvfp4_kernel[grid](
+            x.contiguous(),
+            packed,
+            scales,
+            global_scale,
+            ids.contiguous(),
+            out,
+            num_rows,
+            x.shape[-1],
+            packed.stride(0),
+            scales.stride(0),
+            BLOCK_ROWS=64,
+            BLOCK_BYTES=128,
+        )
+        return out
+    weight = rows[0]
+    _gather_rows_gemv_kernel[grid](
+        x.contiguous(),
+        weight,
+        rows[1] if len(rows) == 2 else weight,
+        ids.contiguous(),
+        out,
+        num_rows,
+        x.shape[-1],
+        weight.stride(0),
+        HAS_SCALE=len(rows) == 2,
+        BLOCK_ROWS=64,
+        BLOCK_HIDDEN=128 if weight.element_size() > 1 else 256,
+    )
+    return out
+

+# Writes the listed and the picked logits into the `-inf` target-vocabulary
+# logits in one launch; columns `[0, num_listed)` of the grid are listed rows,
+# the next `num_picked` are picked rows.
+@triton.jit
+def _scatter_draft_logits_kernel(
+    out_ptr,
+    listed_ptr,
+    token_ids_ptr,
+    picked_ptr,
+    picks_ptr,
+    candidate_ids_ptr,
+    vocab_size,
+    num_listed,
+    num_picked,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    cols = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    is_listed = cols < num_listed
+    is_picked = (cols >= num_listed) & (cols < num_listed + num_picked)
+    pcols = tl.where(is_picked, cols - num_listed, 0)
+    listed_id = tl.load(token_ids_ptr + cols, mask=is_listed, other=0)
+    listed = tl.load(listed_ptr + token * num_listed + cols, mask=is_listed, other=0.0)
+    pick = tl.load(picks_ptr + token * num_picked + pcols, mask=is_picked, other=0)
+    picked_id = tl.load(candidate_ids_ptr + pick, mask=is_picked, other=0)
+    picked = tl.load(picked_ptr + token * num_picked + pcols, mask=is_picked, other=0.0)
+    ids = tl.where(is_listed, listed_id, picked_id).to(tl.int64)
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + token * vocab_size + ids,
+        tl.where(is_listed, listed, picked),
+        mask=is_listed | is_picked,
+    )
+
+
+def scatter_draft_logits(
+    vocab_size: int,
+    listed: torch.Tensor,
+    token_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    picked: torch.Tensor,
+    picks: torch.Tensor,
+    candidate_ids: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Target-vocabulary logits, `-inf` outside the listed and picked rows.
+
+    `out[n, token_ids] = listed[n]` and `out[n, candidate_ids[picks[n]]] =
+    picked[n]`, in one kernel on CUDA.
+    """
+    out = listed.new_full((listed.shape[0], vocab_size), float("-inf"))
+    if not listed.is_cuda:
+        out[:, token_ids] = listed
+        out.scatter_(1, candidate_ids[picks], picked)
+        return out
+    num_listed, num_picked = listed.shape[1], picked.shape[1]
+    block = 1024
+    grid = (listed.shape[0], triton.cdiv(num_listed + num_picked, block))
+    _scatter_draft_logits_kernel[grid](
+        out,
+        listed.contiguous(),
+        token_ids,
+        picked.contiguous(),
+        picks.contiguous(),
+        candidate_ids,
+        vocab_size,
+        num_listed,
+        num_picked,
+        BLOCK=block,
+    )
+    return out
+

+class DraftVocab:
+    """Draft logits over a subset of the target vocabulary.
+
+    Args:
+        logits_processor: Logits processor of the draft lm_head.
+        vocab_size: Target vocabulary size. A smaller draft vocabulary gets a
+            `draft_id_to_target_id` parameter for the model to register and
+            load.
+
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, logits_processor: LogitsProcessor, vocab_size: int):
+        self.logits_processor = logits_processor
+        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
+        self.draft_id_to_target_id: nn.Parameter | None = None
+        if logits_processor.vocab_size < vocab_size:
+            self.draft_id_to_target_id = nn.Parameter(
+                torch.zeros(logits_processor.vocab_size, dtype=torch.long),
+                requires_grad=False,
+            )
+        # Set by load_token_map.
+        self.token_ids: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.rows: _Rows | None = None
+        self.num_dynamic_rows = 0
+
+    def compute_logits(
+        self, lm_head: VocabParallelEmbedding, hidden_states: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Target-vocabulary logits, `-inf` outside the draft vocabulary."""
+        if self.token_ids is not None:
+            listed, picked = self._token_map_logits(hidden_states)
+            if picked is not None:
+                return scatter_draft_logits(
+                    self.vocab_size, listed, self.token_ids, *picked, self.candidate_ids
+                )
+            out = listed.new_full((listed.shape[0], self.vocab_size), float("-inf"))
+            out[:, self.token_ids] = listed
+            return out
+
+        logits = self.logits_processor(lm_head, hidden_states)
+        if self.draft_id_to_target_id is None:
+            return logits
+        base = torch.arange(logits.shape[-1], device=logits.device)
+        targets = base + self.draft_id_to_target_id
+        out = logits.new_full((logits.shape[0], self.vocab_size), float("-inf"))
+        out[:, targets] = logits
+        return out

+    def get_top_tokens(
+        self, lm_head: VocabParallelEmbedding, hidden_states: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:

+        if self.token_ids is not None:
+            listed, picked = self._token_map_logits(hidden_states)
+            listed_max, listed_col = listed.max(dim=-1)
+            top = self.token_ids[listed_col]
+            if picked is None:
+                return top
+            logits, picks = picked
+            picked_max, picked_col = logits.max(dim=-1)
+            pick = picks.gather(1, picked_col.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
+            # Ties go to the listed row, as an argmax over [listed, picked] would.
+            return torch.where(listed_max >= picked_max, top, self.candidate_ids[pick])
+
+        top = self.logits_processor.get_top_tokens(lm_head, hidden_states)
+        return self.map_draft_to_target(top)
+
+    def map_draft_to_target(self, draft_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Target ids of draft-vocabulary ids from the pruned lm_head."""
+        if self.draft_id_to_target_id is None:
+            return draft_ids
+        return draft_ids + self.draft_id_to_target_id[draft_ids]
+
+    def load_token_map(

+    ) -> None:

+        The rows are copied out of `lm_head`, so the drafter keeps sharing it

+

Hi @stecasta, we tried this on our TP2 setup (2× DGX Spark, eager, MTP k=4, nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, MRV2) with dynamic rows extended to TP>1. Two things came up:

2. **Dynamic rows at TP>1:** we all-reduce the Gram once so every rank uses the same basis. Each rank picks `ceil(rows / tp)` off-list rows from its own shard, and greedy drafting reduces local `(logit, id)` pairs with one small all-gather, so no per-token id exchange is needed. Probabilistic drafting with dynamic rows is still rejected at TP>1.
